issues.body: The IPvFuture tail at the `literal_ok` branch still calls `is_iunreserved`, whose definition includes RFC 3987 `ucschar`. IPvFuture is inherited from RFC 3986 and its tail is restricted to ASCII `unreserved / sub-delims / ":"`; RFC 3987 does not widen that production. Consequently `http://[v1.π]/datatype` is still accepted by `is_well_formed_absolute_iri` and can pass authored datatype validation, despite being malformed. This is materially the same major finding as round 3.
issues.fix_hint: Introduce an ASCII RFC 3986 `unreserved` predicate and use it specifically for the IPvFuture tail. Add `http://[v1.π]/datatype` to `MALFORMED`, retain an adjacent valid case such as `http://[v7.host]/datatype`, and add a public expansion regression expecting `InvalidTypedValue` for the malformed datatype.
issues.title: IPvFuture validation still accepts non-ASCII host characters

verdict.summary: Round 4 is stagnant. The round-3 major finding remains unchanged: the IPvFuture tail is still validated with the RFC 3987 `is_iunreserved` predicate, which admits non-ASCII `ucschar`, although RFC 3986 IPvFuture permits only ASCII `unreserved / sub-delims / ":"`. The new corpus still lacks the reported malformed non-ASCII IPvFuture and the public expansion-path regression, so `http://[v1.π]/datatype` remains accepted as a datatype IRI. The surrounding IPv6 and valid IPvFuture tests do not exercise this boundary.
